first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 EPS $0.06 on revenue $11.4-11.6m. Chartmill: $0.06 / $11.598m (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/BOSC/estimates, via search snippet; the page returns 403 when fetched). Benzinga: $0.06 / $11.4m (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BOSC/earnings-forecasts, via snippet). Finviz 'EPS next Q' 0.06 (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=BOSC). Three analysts; FY2026 EPS $0.54 as of 2026-11-07. EPS agrees across three sources, revenue is within $0.2m. Company guide: FY2026 revenue >$51m, net income >$3.6m (Q2 release https://finviz.com/news/384037/bos-reports-second-quarter-and-first-half-2026-financial-results), restated on 2026-11-17 as 'exceed 2025 levels' (2025: revenue $50.6m, net income $3.6m). For comparison: Q3 2025 was $11.4m revenue, $0.677m net income, $0.11 EPS (https://finviz.com/news/238315/bos-continues-record-year-performance-in-q3-2025-sales-increase-16-year-over-year), and Q2 2026 was $14.9m and $0.19 against a $0.13 consensus.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is 22,500 shares, 0.7 days to cover (shortsqueeze.com, page dated 2026-10-22, https://shortsqueeze.com/?symbol=BOSC). Finviz shows 0.14% short float and a 0.25 short ratio (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=BOSC, read 2026-11-27). Not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism. There is no options market (baseline options.status = no_options_market), so there is no skew. Tape (Yahoo chart): close 4.43 on 2026-11-27, 20-day run-up +1.14%, 5-day +2.55%, 13.8% below the 52-week high; average volume about 58k shares a day, roughly $0.26m a day. On 2026-11-05 the stock fell 7.55% (4.24 to 3.92) on 124k shares, the same day as a $650k order release; I found no cause. Since the 2026-11-13 close of 4.02 it has recovered about 10%, including +2.65% on 1.4x volume on the 2026-11-17 backlog release. Market cap is about $31m, trailing P/E about 8, one Street target at $8.

evidence.text: On 2026-11-17, with Q3 already closed and 13 days before the print, BOS restated that full-year 2026 revenue AND net income will 'exceed 2025 levels' (>$50.6m and >$3.6m). H1 net income was $2.1m, so H2 must be above $1.5m. The Q3 consensus of $0.06 EPS (about $0.42m on 7.06m shares) would leave Q4 needing about $1.1m+, above any quarter except Q2 2026's $1.4m. Q4 has only $11m of scheduled backlog deliveries. Reaffirming net income with Q3 already known therefore points to Q3 net income nearer $0.6-0.8m, about $0.08-0.11 EPS, against the $0.06 bar. Operating leverage is high: opex is about $2.3m a quarter and gross margin 23-24%, so each $1m of revenue above $11.5m adds about $0.03 of EPS.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS against consensus has moved this name in both directions. Q2 2026 (2026-08-20): $0.19 vs $0.13 consensus, +3.5% (4.53 to 4.69). Q1 2026 (2026-05-28): $0.11 vs $0.14 with revenue down y/y, -9.7%. Q3 2025 (2025-11-25): beat plus guide raise, +10.1%. Q1 2025 (2025-05-29): record $15m revenue, +19.8%. Q4 2025 (2026-03-31): 2026 guide flat on 2025, -10.2%. Closes from the Yahoo chart v8 daily bars.
evidence.why_not_priced: The $0.06 Q3 consensus (Chartmill, Benzinga, finviz) sits below Q3 2025's $0.11 even after the company restated its net-income guide with Q3 known. If the market had done this arithmetic, the three estimate sources would have moved up after 2026-11-17, and Chartmill's latest FY revision is dated 2026-11-07, before the release. The stock rose only +2.65% on the release, which the headline backlog alone could explain. With three analysts and $0.26m of daily turnover, nobody may have redone the H2 split.
evidence.independence: Shares one document with finding 2 (the backlog release). Separate support: Q2 management said gross margin should rise because prices have been raised since early 2026 (Q2 call transcript, https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262122051-tradingkey), and the shekel weakened in Q3 (finding 3). This is an inference from the guide, not a reported Q3 number.

evidence.text: The Q3-end backlog is a record $35m, up from $31m at Q2 end and $24m at year-end 2025. Its timing has shifted: about $24m is scheduled for 2027 and only about $11m for Q4 2026, against about $11m beyond 2026 and $20m due in H2 2026 at Q2 end. That is roughly $13m of new 2027-dated orders in one quarter, so 2027 starts with deliveries equal to about 47% of 2026's guided revenue already contracted. It also means the Q4 revenue that closes the >$51m guide must partly come from orders booked and shipped within the quarter. The video call will likely be asked about 2027.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog headlines have not reliably moved the stock. Backlog was flat at $31m in Q2 2026 and the stock still rose +3.5% on the EPS beat. The Q1 2026 backlog jump to $31m (+29%) came with a -9.7% day because revenue fell. This release itself bought +2.65% on 2026-11-17.
evidence.why_not_priced: The headline ($35m, +45%) is public and partly priced. What is not in any summary I found is the timing split compared with Q2-end: aggregators carry the headline, and no preview compares $11m for Q4 with the $20m due in H2 at Q2 end. If 2027 visibility were priced, the stock would not sit at about 8x trailing earnings and 13.8% below its 52-week high on a record backlog.
evidence.independence: Shares one document with finding 1. Q2-end timing from the Q2 call coverage (https://pulse2.com/bos-backlog-holds-at-record-31-million-despite-30-sequential-revenue-growth/) and Q2 release. Q3 order releases with 2027 delivery: $1.2m European defense (2026-09-16, 2027-28 delivery), $380k robotics follow-on (2026-10-01, 2027), $2.3m Israeli defense (2026-09-01, $1.6m in 2027) (https://finviz.com/news/387492/bos-secures-23-million-order-from-a-leading-israeli-defense-customer).

evidence.text: The shekel weakened about 2.9% against the US dollar in Q3 2026, after strengthening about 5.9% in Q2 (Bank of Israel Q3 FX market report). The CFO had put the H1 2026 opex hit from dollar weakness at about $0.6m, so Q3 should carry less of that drag than Q2's exit rate. This is a small tailwind for Q3 net income relative to the run rate the consensus was built on.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated reaction to FX. FX was cited as the reason the net-income guide was held, not raised, at Q1 2026 (-9.7% day).
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a macro-to-company link the company has not confirmed. The Q3 average rate relative to the Q2 average is unknown, since the quarter-on-quarter change is end-of-period. Small by construction; a proxy.
evidence.independence: Proxy. The CFO quantified the H1 drag in the Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/384037/bos-reports-second-quarter-and-first-half-2026-financial-results). No company statement on Q3 FX.

evidence.text: The 2026-11-17 release, written with Q3 known, kept the full-year guide at 'exceed 2025 levels' rather than raising it. So the print most likely carries a reaffirmation, not the kind of raise that bought +10.1% on 2025-11-25. On this name a flat guide was sold (-10.2% on 2026-03-31).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide raise on 2025-11-25: +10.1%. Guide flat on 2025 levels on 2026-03-31: -10.2%. Revenue guide raised to 'exceed $51m' but net income held on 2026-05-28: -9.7%. Net-income guide raised on 2026-08-20: +3.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the language has been public for ten days, and this lands inside what the company already guided, so it is sized toward 0. The residual risk is that the print's headline reads as 'guidance reiterated' on a name whose holders have sold reiterations.
evidence.independence: Same document as findings 1 and 2. The readings fit together: Q3 decent enough to reaffirm net income (finding 1), but no raise (this finding). The pattern of reactions to raises versus reiterations comes from the Yahoo chart closes cited above.

evidence.text: Q3 order releases: $1.9m air-defense POs (2026-08-04), $1.8m semiconductor connectors (2026-08-10), $2.3m Israeli defense (2026-09-01, $0.7m in 2026), $1.2m European defense (2026-09-16), $990k US (2026-07-23, Q4/Q1 delivery)
Robotics orders after the quarter: $380k follow-on (2026-10-01, 2027 delivery) and $650k munitions packing line (2026-11-05, 2027 delivery)

first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 EPS $0.04 (Chartmill: $0.04 EPS, $21.53M revenue, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/HMR/estimates; Benzinga: $0.04 EPS, $22.5M revenue, last updated Nov 2, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HMR/earnings-forecasts). Both are SNIPPET ONLY because both pages return 403 to a fetch. The two agree on EPS and differ slightly on revenue. The prior quarter's bar was disputed: Earnings Whispers had $0.10 and Quiver $0.05 for Q2, against a $0.04 actual. There is no company guidance. Reference points: Q2 2026 revenue $29.0M, adj. net income $2.4M ($0.04), from the company PDF https://www.heidmar.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/HMR-PR-Q2-2026-EARNINGS.pdf; Q3 2025 revenue $15.6M, adj. net income $1.8M, https://rss.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/11/06/3183125/0/en/Heidmar-Maritime-Holdings-Corp-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results.html. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on EPS, roughly $0.05 expected against $0.04. The revenue bar looks stale, about 25% below Q2's actual.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is 16,021 shares: 0.27% of float, 0.03% of shares outstanding, 0.14 days to cover (stockanalysis.com statistics, fetched 2026-11-27, no settlement date shown, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/hmr/statistics/). The sweep's June/July figure was 2.1-2.9%. There is no crowded short, so no squeeze cushion under a negative. Float is 6.04M of 58.99M shares; insiders hold 89.8%, the CEO about 26.3M via Rhea Marine. There is no options market, so no skew. The tape (stockanalysis history): 0.93 on Nov 23, then +15.05% (Nov 24, vol 233k), +13.08% (Nov 25, vol 130k) and +20.66% (Nov 27 half-day, vol 583k, about 10% of float) to 1.46. Before that the stock fell -23.6% on Oct 30 on no news, from a 1.91 high on Oct 13. Baseline: run_up_5d +44.55%, run_up_20d -17.98%, realised vol 151.8%.

evidence.text: HMR rose 57% in three sessions into the print, from 0.93 (Nov 23) to 1.46 (Nov 27 half-day close: +15.05%, +13.08%, +20.66%). The Nov 27 half-day traded 583k shares, about 10% of the 6.04M float. There was no company release or SEC filing after Sep 9, and Tickeron found no company catalyst (sector backdrop only, 'news significance 30/100'). So the stock enters a bmo print with a speculative premium on a stock that was 0.93 four sessions ago.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2026, the closest analog: 1.16 to 1.50 (+29%) on May 22 into the May 26 Q1 release, 1.57 on May 26, then 1.25 on May 27 (-20.4%) and 1.14 on May 28 (Yahoo chart bars). The run built before the print and unwound within two sessions.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, not a fact the price missed. The question is whether the premium survives the release. If the market had already discounted a sell-the-news unwind, the stock would not have closed at the high of the run on the heaviest volume in a month. Nothing explains the run (no 6-K, no fleet release, no filing on EDGAR since Sep 9), so it has to be validated by the release or unwind.
evidence.independence: The Tickeron blog (https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-heidmar-maritime-holdings-corp-hmr-stock-up-15-70-today-48436/, 2026-11-27) confirms the Nov 27 move had no company catalyst and cites a ~6M float. EDGAR's filing list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0002029471) shows nothing after 2026-09-09. This finding and the reaction-history finding both point to sell-the-news, but they rest on different data (this run vs prior prints).

evidence.text: The last three prints were all sold on release. Q4 2025 (Mar 24, 2026): 0.902 to 0.856, -5.1%, then -4.6% the next day. Q1 2026 (May 26): +4.7% on the day after a +29% pre-print spike, then -20.4% on May 27. Q2 2026 (Sep 1, bmo): 1.39 to 1.24, -10.8%. The Q2 sell-off came despite revenue of $29.0M against a ~$21.4-24.4M consensus and bullish rate commentary.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This finding is the reaction history: three of three prints in 2026 closed lower within two sessions. The Q2 revenue beat with an EPS miss against a disputed $0.10 bar was sold -10.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The baseline carries no reaction history: the 6-K archive was unread, so n=0. A market that had priced this pattern would not bid the stock 57% into the release. The reaction function exists only in the daily bars, which no aggregator summarises for this name.
evidence.independence: The Q2 reaction is independently reported as 'Heidmar Maritime Stock Down 10.8%' (dailypolitical aggregator snippet, https://www.dailypolitical.com/?p=10489932, 403 to fetch). Release dates come from https://www.heidmar.com/news/. The pre-print-spike pattern overlaps conceptually with the run-up finding but uses different data.

evidence.text: Q3 EPS should come in at or above the $0.04 bar, and revenue should clear the stale $21.5-22.5M consensus. Q2 revenue was $29.0M: trade revenues $5.80M plus voyage/time-charter $23.20M. Q3 adds Q-Shipping management fees (nine managed vessels from Jul 1, three more taken over in Q3) on a ~60-vessel commercially managed fleet. Q2 G&A of $5.57M included $1.8M of cash bonuses, against Q1 G&A of about $3.56M. If Q3 G&A normalises, operating income gains about $1.5M on a Q2 base of $1.82M.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 revenue beat (29.0 vs ~21.4-24.4M) came with an EPS miss against a disputed bar and was sold -10.8%. This name has not paid for revenue beats.
evidence.why_not_priced: The revenue consensus ($21.5-22.5M) sits 25% below the last actual, which suggests the 2-3 estimates have not been rebuilt for the relet business and Q-Shipping. The EPS bar rests on snippets only, and the prior-quarter bar was disputed (EW $0.10 vs Quiver $0.05), so the size is capped small.
evidence.independence: Q-Shipping completion and the nine-vessel addition are confirmed separately by https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/heidmar-maritime-holdings-corp-expands-ship-management-platform-2026-07-07 (2026-07-07). The G&A bonus timing is from the same Q2 PDF, not independent.

evidence.text: Peers that reported after Heidmar last spoke show Q4 2026 mid-size tanker bookings at extremes: Teekay Tankers has 58% of Q4 Suezmax spot days at $272,000/day and Aframax/LR2 at $208,300, against Q3 averages of $106,437 and $67,552; DHT has 50% of Q4 VLCC spot days at $509,100. Heidmar runs Suezmax/Aframax pools and earns commissions on pool gross, and in September it guided that 'rates to remain elevated and potentially strengthen further' in Q4/Q1. The Nov 30 call is the first time it can quantify Q4 pool earnings.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 (Sep 1) carried similar bullish rate commentary ('Suezmaxes in the Mediterranean / Black Sea are at historical highs') and the stock fell -10.8%. Forward commentary has not been paid for at this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Peer rates have been public since Oct 12 (DHT) and Nov 12 (Teekay), yet HMR fell from 1.91 to 0.93 over the same period, so the market has not mapped tanker rates onto HMR's commission line. A Heidmar-specific Q4 pool figure on the call would be new. This is macro-to-company transmission that the company has confirmed only qualitatively, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: DHT Q4 bookings: https://finviz.com/news/401131/dht-holdings-reports-q3-fleet-earnings-of-141300-per-day-as-fourth-quarter-tanker-rates-rise (2026-10-12). Company's own Q4 expectation: Q2 PDF p.3 (2026-09-01).

evidence.text: Q3 realised mid-size spot rates fell slightly from Q2 at the closest listed peer: Teekay Suezmax $106,437 vs $109,171 (-2.5%), Aframax/LR2 $67,552 vs $74,149 (-8.9%). Heidmar's Q3 pool commissions and relet margins (Q2: voyage/TC revenue $23.2M against charter-in and other $21.4M) therefore have no rate tailwind quarter on quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No HMR-specific history of reacting to rate-driven misses. Prior prints were sold regardless of the rate backdrop.
evidence.why_not_priced: A peer proxy for the Q3 line. Its scale is offset by fleet growth (finding 3), so it is small. The Clarksons index reportedly showed record Q3 Suezmax averages, which points the other way and could not be verified (see rejected).
evidence.independence: Shares the Teekay article with the Q4 finding. This finding reads the Q3 line, the other the Q4 bookings; they are separate lines from one document, sized apart.

evidence.text: Heidmar has a $20M committed equity purchase facility with B. Riley Principal Capital II, under which up to 11,080,332 shares are registered for resale. The POS AM went effective June 10, 2026, and the facility runs 36 months. The company can sell shares at its discretion into a spike, and BRPC II resells them. Against a 6.04M float this is a supply overhang on a +57% run. The company has no visible need for the money: $28.7M cash, positive operating cash flow of $7.7M in H1, an asset-light model, and no acquisition named.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no disclosed draw. Weighted basic shares rose only from 58.24M (Q2'25) to 59.59M (Q2'26), so usage looks minimal so far.
evidence.why_not_priced: The facility is public, but the share count moving on the Q3 balance sheet or in the subsequent-events note would be new. Asked what the money buys: nothing corroborated, but the company is not in distress either, so the negative is small and rests on supply, not solvency.
evidence.independence: EDGAR EFFECT notice dated 2026-06-10 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0002029471). Same underlying facility.

evidence.text: The CEO (Pankaj Khanna, also a 10% owner via Rhea Marine at 26.24M shares) filed Form 4s, late, for small purchases: 20,000 shares at $1.22 (Jun 24) and 15,000 at $1.30 (Sep 1, the Q2 print day), about $44k in total. Form 144 proposed sales were filed by other holders on Jun 11, Jun 26 and Jul 6.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell -10.8% on the day the CEO bought.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public since September and tiny relative to the holding. It is a token signal and is sized near zero.

evidence.text: Director Andreas Konialidis stepped down on Oct 13, 2026, with 'no disagreement'. The company said it would search for a replacement 'in due course'. This is the only company release between the Q2 print and the Q3 date notice.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public for six weeks. It matters only if the call names a replacement or ties the departure to a holder exit.

evidence.text: Clarksons: Q3 2026 ClarkSea Index at a record $46,384/day, Suezmax at a record $228,262/day, Aframax $119,189/day, MR rising to ~$60k by quarter-end. This would point to a strong Q3 pool-commission line.
Mirror-site pages (bvwd.ca.gov and others) claiming 'Q4 2025 EPS miss, shares fall 23.1%' and 'surges 29%' around prints
Kalkine: 'HMR surges as small-cap tanker names ride firmer crude' and 'jumped with no confirmed catalyst'
Analyst price targets of $3.00 (2 analysts, Buy) and $5.00 (Benzinga)
EDGAR filing list for CIK 0002029471: no 6-K, F-3, 424B or 13D after 2026-09-09, so no financing, fleet or holder filing explains the Nov 24-27 run
Company news page heidmar.com/news: nothing between Oct 14 (board) and Nov 11 (date notice), and nothing after
Explanation for the Oct 30 -23.6% drop: Tickeron and Benzinga found no catalyst
Reliable Q1 2026 consensus and Q4 2025 consensus: only spam mirror pages
Kalkine articles on the November jumps: 403 on fetch
Earnings Whispers Q3 article: no consensus figure on the page
Clarksons Q3 2026 index article (seatrade-maritime): 403 on fetch

evidence.text: Q3 2026 TCE will come in below Q2. In the Aug 27 report NAT said about 75% of Q3 fleet days were booked at about $54,000/day, with the rest at spot of $60-90k/day. That blends to roughly $57-62k/day against Q2's $63,000/day, so the per-share dividend most likely steps down from Q2's $0.27 (Q1 paid $0.22 on $46.3m net). NAT headlines the dividend every quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No reliable dated reaction found. The baseline history is untrustworthy (6-K letters counted as prints). Scraped pages put the Q4 2025 reaction at roughly -2.4% to +3.2%, in conflict with one another and not reliable.
